china-1925-6:p0450_1.rationale: Packages, weight and letters carried for Minchu (private letter) agencies by year; a postal service series.

china-1925-6:p0452_1.rationale: Chinese Post Office staff by rank in 1908 and 1924. Personnel of a postal service, with no matching staff-specific tag.
review_questions: Should a tag for postal or public-service personnel be proposed? government-offices is a poor fit for a postal operating workforce.

china-1925-6:p0453_1.rationale: Foreign employees of the Chinese Post Office by nationality. The subject is postal staff composition, so population is not added.
review_questions: Is a postal-staff tag needed? nationality-and-ethnicity was not assigned because the table counts employees, not residents.

china-1925-6:p0455_1.rationale: Number of post offices taking part in international C.O.D. parcel exchange, grouped by partner countries. Statistical.

china-1925-6:p0456_1.rationale: Growth of offices, articles and parcels posted, and courier and steamer lines, 1906-1923.

china-1925-6:p0456_2.rationale: Cash-on-delivery parcels handled by the post office: number, value and weight by year.

china-1925-6:p0457_1.rationale: International comparison of mail volumes (letters, postcards, printed matter) and per-head averages. Population appears only as a denominator.

china-1925-6:p0457_2.rationale: Categories of money order offices with their issue and cashing limits, in dollars. Postal money-order system.

china-1925-6:p0457_3.rationale: Value of money orders issued and cashed by the Chinese Post Office by year.

china-1925-6:p0458_1.rationale: Postal service income, working expenditure, surplus and capital expenditure, 1914-23. An operating account of the post office, so not a public budget.
review_questions: Should a tag be proposed for public enterprise accounts? public-budgets was not used because this is a service operating account.
